sources.name: IEEE Computer Society: Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK) v4.0a
sources.applies_to_note: Set from the page content: the engineering half of the role (software construction, architecture, testing, operations, security).
sources.rationale: The professional society's consensus body of knowledge for software engineering. Forward-deployed engineer has no body of its own, so its engineering side borrows from SWEBOK (approved in the proposal).
sources.licence: User License Agreement on the SWEBOK page: "You may quote or reproduce reasonable passages from SWEBOK 4.0 in a review, article, scholarly, or educational material, provided that you provide an appropriate citation to the source document." It also says "You may not post SWEBOK version 4.0 publicly, or provide any manner of public access to your downloaded document, including through links." (so cite the computer.org page, never link a copy of the PDF)
sources.free_parts: overview, FAQs and terms are open; the guide PDF is reached through a download page (reported as an email form, not observed)

last_verified.how: opened the SWEBOK overview page and the download page without credentials; the guide PDF was not downloaded
last_verified.note: The overview page (about 28,000 characters: scope, FAQs, terms) opens with no login and was read. The download page (…/software-engineering/v4) is script-rendered: no form is visible in a plain fetch, so the email form comes from the proposal and a search result, not from observation. The guide itself was not opened, so its text was not read.

sources.quotable: yes for reasonable passages with citation, per the license text on the page; the guide itself was not opened
sources.decision_note: Attributed citation only: short quotes with clear attribution, pointing the learner to the real page; never full-text reproduction (same approach as the owner decision of 2026-10-16 for documents with no stated reuse terms).
